title: Chain-level signed product Hom comparison with a source mapping cone
statement:
Let $\mathcal A,\mathcal B,\mathcal C$ be abelian categories [def-sp-abelian], with countable products in $\mathcal C$, and let $H:\mathcal A^{\mathrm{op}}\to(\mathcal B\to\mathcal C)$ be separately additive. Fix a cochain complex $I$ of $\mathcal B$. For a cochain complex $V$ of $\mathcal A$ define $U(V)^n=\prod_{p\in\mathbf Z}H(V^p,I^{p+n})$, with differential on the $(p,q)$ projection, $q=p+n+1$, given by $(-1)^p(H(V^p,d_I)\pi_{p,q-1}-H(d_V,I^q)\pi_{p+1,q})$. Write $U(g)$ for componentwise precomposition by a chain map $g$. Take a chain map $f:K\to L$, and put $E=\operatorname{Cone}(f)$, $E^p=L^p\oplus K^{p+1}$, $d_E(l,k)=(d_Ll+f(k),-d_Kk)$, with shifts as in [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Set $X=U(L)$, $Y=U(K)$ and $t=U(f):X\to Y$.

For each $n$, restrict the $p$-th product component of $U(E)^n$ along the two biproduct inclusions, and denote the resulting components by $x_p\in H(L^p,I^{p+n})$ and $a_p\in H(K^{p+1},I^{p+n})$. This notation means equations of morphisms after projection, not elements of an arbitrary abelian category. There is a natural chain isomorphism
$$\theta_f:U(E)\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Cone}(t)[-1]$$
whose degree-$n$ components, in the order $Y^{n-1}\oplus X^n$, are $(y,x)$ with $y_j=(-1)^{j-1}a_{j-1}$ and $x_p=x_p$. Its inverse has $a_p=(-1)^p y_{p+1}$. Under this isomorphism the differential of $U(E)$ is
$$ (y,x)\longmapsto(-d_Yy-tx,\ d_Xx),$$
and the restriction $U(i):U(E)\to X$, for $i:L\to E$, is the projection $(y,x)\mapsto x$. The isomorphism is natural in commuting squares of chain maps $f$. No boundedness, exactness of products, preservation of quasi-isomorphisms, or injectivity of $I$ is assumed.

proof.text: Work throughout with morphisms out of an arbitrary object $T$ of $\mathcal C$; component notation below denotes their composites with product projections. Equality on every projection is equality by the defining uniqueness of products. The preadditive structure and finite biproducts in [def-sp-abelian] allow sums of these morphisms. Write $s_p=(-1)^p$, $D_p=H(V^p,d_I)$ and $A_p=H(d_V^p,I)$, with the target degree understood. The displayed differential is $b'_p=s_p(D_pb_p-A_pb_{p+1})$. Applying it twice gives $D^2b_p-D_pA_pb_{p+1}+A_pD_{p+1}b_{p+1}-A_pA_{p+1}b_{p+2}=0$: the first and last terms vanish by $d_I^2=d_V^2=0$ and additivity, and the middle terms cancel by bifunctoriality. Here $s_p^2=1$ and $s_ps_{p+1}=-1$. Thus the specified differential really defines a complex.

proof.text: For $g:V\to W$, the $p$-component of $U(g)b$ is $H(g^p,I)b_p$. Bifunctoriality commutes this map with $H(-,d_I)$; the chain-map equality $g^{p+1}d_V^p=d_W^pg^p$ commutes it with the second term of the differential. Consequently $U(g)d=dU(g)$ componentwise. Functoriality also gives $U(hg)=U(g)U(h)$ and $U(1)=1$. In particular $t=U(f)$ is a chain map.

proof.text: Let $\iota_L,\iota_K$ and $r_L,r_K$ be the inclusions and projections of $E^p=L^p\oplus K^{p+1}$. At any fixed target degree, restriction by $H(\iota_L,I)$ and $H(\iota_K,I)$ sends a morphism $b:T\to H(E^p,I)$ to $(x,a)$. Conversely $(x,a)$ determines $b=H(r_L,I)x+H(r_K,I)a$. The identities $r_\alpha\iota_\beta=\delta_{\alpha\beta}$ give restriction followed by reconstruction on the two components; $\iota_Lr_L+\iota_Kr_K=1$ and additivity give reconstruction followed by restriction on $b$. These formulas are inverse morphisms in $\mathcal C$, without using any exactness property of $H$.

source.place: Tag 08JC, lemma-RHom-triangulated, proof (details omitted); explicit agent calculation with the signed differential of BifunctorHomComplex.lean:55-76

proof.text: Apply the product universal property to the two restrictions in the previous step. The $x_p$ form a morphism to $X^n$. Set $y_j=s_{j-1}a_{j-1}$, whose target is $H(K^j,I^{j+n-1})$; these form a morphism to $Y^{n-1}$. Pairing them defines $\theta^n:U(E)^n\to Y^{n-1}\oplus X^n$. Conversely, on the projections of $Y^{n-1}\oplus X^n$, set $a_p=s_py_{p+1}$ and reconstruct the $p$-component using the preceding formula. Product uniqueness gives a morphism back to $U(E)^n$. The two composites are identities, since $s_p^2=1$ and the reconstruction formulas are inverse. All products used here are indexed by $\mathbf Z$; reindexing only replaces $p$ by $j-1$. In Lean, construct the forward map directly as a cocycle: let alpha = ofHom(U(inr f)) and beta = -bifunctorHomMapLeftCochain(inl f). The identity delta beta + alpha.comp(ofHom(U(f))) = 0 follows from delta_bifunctorHomMapLeftCochain, mappingCone.delta_inl and contravariant composition. Apply mappingCone.liftCocycle to (alpha,beta), then rightShift by -1 and homOf. The liftCochain projection equations and the signed precomposition projection formula give exactly x and y above. Define the inverse by bifunctorHomLift and the explicit reconstruction in step 3. The two inverse identities follow from mappingCone.id_X, the four inclusion/projection identities and product uniqueness.

proof.text: The cone and shift in [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] give $\operatorname{Cone}(t)[-1]^n=Y^{n-1}\oplus X^n$ and differential $(y,x)\mapsto(-d_Yy-tx,d_Xx)$: the cone differential at degree $n-1$ is $(d_Yy+tx,-d_Xx)$, and shifting by $-1$ negates it. This identifies the graded target of $\theta$ with the complex in the statement, with the required summand order.

source.place: Tag 08JC, lemma-RHom-triangulated, proof (details omitted); explicit agent calculation with the signed differential of BifunctorHomComplex.lean:55-76

proof.text:
Compute $d_{U(E)}$ before the sign change, using the matrix of $d_E$ and additivity. In the restrictions to $L^p$ and $K^{p+1}$ it gives
$$x'_p=s_p\bigl(H(L^p,d_I)x_p-H(d_L^p,I)x_{p+1}\bigr)=(d_Xx)_p,$$
$$a'_p=s_p\bigl(H(K^{p+1},d_I)a_p-H(f^{p+1},I)x_{p+1}+H(d_K^{p+1},I)a_{p+1}\bigr).$$
Indeed $d_E\iota_L=\iota_Ld_L$ and $d_E\iota_K=\iota_Lf-\iota_Kd_K$; applying contravariant $H(-,I)$ reverses these composites and sends the minus to a minus. The outer subtraction in the Hom differential therefore gives the positive $d_K$ term displayed here. Each equation is an equality of composites of morphisms with projections.

source.place: Tag 08JC, lemma-RHom-triangulated, proof (details omitted); explicit agent calculation with the signed differential of BifunctorHomComplex.lean:55-76

proof.text:
For the first output coordinate put $p=j-1$ in the second equation and multiply by $s_{j-1}$. Substituting $a_{j-1}=s_{j-1}y_j$ and $a_j=s_jy_{j+1}$ gives
$$y'_j=s_{j-1}H(K^j,d_I)y_j+s_jH(d_K^j,I)y_{j+1}-H(f^j,I)x_j=-(d_Yy)_j-(tx)_j.$$
The first equation already gives $x'=d_Xx$. Hence $\theta^{n+1}d_{U(E)}=d_{\operatorname{Cone}(t)[-1]}\theta^n$ on every projection, and therefore as morphisms. Its graded inverse is a chain map as well: multiplying this equality on the left and right by the degreewise inverses gives $d_{U(E)}(\theta^n)^{-1}=(\theta^{n+1})^{-1}d_{\operatorname{Cone}(t)[-1]}$. Thus $\theta$ is a chain isomorphism, rather than merely a family of isomorphisms on cohomology. The Lean cocycle construction in step 4 packages this chain-map verification through the existing delta_bifunctorHomMapLeftCochain identity. For the displayed y-differential formula, evaluate that identity on inl f at (n,n), use delta_inl and U(f followed by inr f) = U(inr f) followed by U(f), and solve the resulting additive equation. The x-differential is the chain-map equation for U(inr f). Use HomologicalComplex.Hom.isoOfComponents with the explicit degreewise inverse; no object is chosen from an existence statement.

source.place: Tag 08JC, lemma-RHom-triangulated, proof (details omitted); explicit agent calculation with the signed differential of BifunctorHomComplex.lean:55-76

proof.text: Restriction by $i:L\to E$ is exactly restriction along $\iota_L$ in every degree, so $U(i)$ is $(y,x)\mapsto x$. For naturality take $u:K\to K'$, $v:L\to L'$ with $vf=f'u$. The cone map $c:E\to E'$ has degreewise matrix $\operatorname{diag}(v^p,u^{p+1})$. Thus $U(c)$ sends $(x'_p,a'_p)$ to $(H(v^p,I)x'_p,H(u^{p+1},I)a'_p)$. After $y_j=s_{j-1}a_{j-1}$ this becomes $(U(u)y',U(v)x')$, the shifted cone map from $\operatorname{Cone}(U(f'))[-1]$ to $\operatorname{Cone}(U(f))[-1]$. This proves the naturality square on every projection, including its direction. Every construction used only addition, the stated biproducts and countable products, so none of the extra hypotheses explicitly excluded in the statement is needed. In Lean, expand mappingCone.map through mappingCone.desc_f to verify its two projection equations before shifting; transport those equations through shiftFunctorObjXIso using XIsoOfEq_hom_naturality. Naturality then follows by signedCone_to_ext and bifunctorHomObj_hom_ext, with the source-cone map equations obtained from mappingCone.inl_v_desc_f and mappingCone.inr_f_desc_f.
